recs.title: Borescope cylinders and exhaust valves - *HIGHLY RECOMMENDED*
recs.detail:
While standard differential compression tests can easily miss an exhaust valve on the verge of failure, high-definition borescopic inspections provide the definitive look inside your engine to prevent catastrophic breakdowns. Our visual inspection evaluates cylinder barrel condition, piston crowns, and valve thermal health—identifying early signs of heat distress, such as asymmetrical deposit patterns or green hot spots, long before a valve burns through. Because an exhaust valve relies on physical seat contact to shed up to 80% of its heat, catching uneven seating early allows for minor, low-cost remediation like in-place lapping rather than a multi-thousand-dollar cylinder replacement or in-flight emergency. 

By establishing a digital trend-monitoring baseline at regular oil changes or annuals, you protect your investment, avoid massive repair bills, and fly with complete confidence in your engine’s reliability.

recs.title: Rocketlink steering link
recs.detail: While traditional tailwheel chains and loose external springs suffer from slop, sag, and sluggish rudder response, the Rocket Steering Link delivers crisp, positive ground handling by replacing flexible hardware with an engineered, internal-spring telescoping linkage. Designed for high-performance taildraggers, this precision link provides immediate, direct steering feedback during taxiing while absorbing severe shock loads and preserving smooth, predictable full-swivel unlocking for tight ramp maneuvering. By eliminating chain stretch, binding, and the slop-induced wear that chews up tailwheel locking pins and control arms, it prevents erratic directional wander during high-speed rollouts and crosswind landings. Eliminating sloppy ground control before it leads to an unexpected swerve or ground loop protects you from catastrophic prop strikes, bent wingtips, and multi-thousand-dollar airframe repair bills—giving you absolute authority and confidence whenever your tailwheel meets the runway.
recs.broch:
RV Rocket Steering Link
 
The RV Rocket Steering Link was invented by Terry Jantzi, an award-winning RV-6 builder. It will fit the RV-4, RV-6, RV-7, RV-8, RV-9,, Harmon Rocket II, and the F1 Rocket. The RV-14 has a different tail spring from the other RV lines, which may change the geometry somewhat... this item may be adaptable to the RV-14 but may require some modifications.

Bolt-on installation consists of replacing the chains-and-springs with the steering link and control arm. All of the hardware is included. You get everything necessary for quick installation: steering link, control arm, and rod ends. This item now ships standard with a Tie-down control arm, giving you a handy place to tie down your tail.

The RV Rocket Steering Link is a good way to tidy up the tail end of your aircraft. It weighs less and it is a simple way to replace those draggy-looking chains and springs.

We can't promise that it will make you go faster, but it might make your friends believe that it does!

How can I tell if I have the stock Vans tailspring and full locking tailwheel?
If your tailwheel pivots 360 degrees, you have a full swivel tailwheel. If your tailwheel locks and unlocks then you have a locking tailwheel. If your tailwheel assembly looks like a Van's assembly and the vertical shaft is 7/8 inches in diameter you probably have a Vans unit.

What if my vertical shaft diameter is 3/4 inches?
Some of the older RV-4 or RV-6 kits were converted from a non-swivel tailwheel and an Aviation Products tailwheel was used. The tailwheel assembly will look like the Vans product but the vertical shaft diameter is 3/4 inches. We do have control arms available that will fit the Aviation Products tailwheel. Order that item here. If you need the API control arm, you can select "No control arm" on this item and then add the API arm to your cart separately.

Is there any measurement I can take to assure the RV Rocket Steering Link will fit my aircraft?
Measure the distance from the center of the hole in the rudder horn (the aft hole) to the center of the hole in the steering arm while the rudder and tailwheel are in trail. If you have a measurement between 13 and 13-1/2 inches then the standard size Steering Link will fit.

What does it mean if the measurement is not between 13 and 13-1/2 inches?
It means your kit has been modified. The older RV4 and RV6 kits came with a non-swivel tailwheel. Some of these kits were modified to take a full swivel locking tailwheel. In the modification process, the tail spring was cut. In most of the cases I have seen on these modified units, the distance between rudder horn and control arm can be as short as 12 1/4 inches and as much as 14 1/4 inches. In these cases, we may be able to work with you to get a special size made or make recommendations for making the standard size work. Please contact us for more information.

Why would I order with no control arm?
If you already have a single-sided control arm for whatever reason, if you are ordering this link along with a tailwheel mounting kit (which includes a control arm), or if you're ordering an API control arm separately, you can order this link without the arm included. We do not recommend that you use an existing double-sided control arm with this product. The Steering Link control arm features a twist in the arm by design, which you would not have if using a standard double-sided arm.
recs.res: Removed steering link springs and replaced with Flyboys Rocketlink steering link.  Installation completed in accordance with manufacturer provided instructions.

recs.title: Condor tailwheel
recs.detail: While traditional solid-rubber tailwheels slam brutal impact loads into your airframe when operating on unpaved runways, the Condor pneumatic tailwheel provides the ultimate shock absorption, ground clearance, and flotation required for effortless grass strip flying. Replacing harsh, hard-cured tires with a cushioned, high-pressure pneumatic tire and swept fork geometry, the Condor glides smoothly over turf ruts, humps, and soft soil while absorbing peak impact forces before they reach your airframe. This dramatic reduction in ground shock protects your tail spring, aft bulkhead, and fuselage rivets from severe stress and metal fatigue, eliminating the cumulative jarring that leads to micro-cracking, loose rivets, and premature tail assembly failure. Upgrading to a pneumatic tailwheel for off-airport and grass field operations safeguards your airframe against multi-thousand-dollar tailcone structural repairs and unexpected groundings—delivering butter-smooth ground handling, precise steering, and total confidence whenever you operate off the pavement.
recs.broch:
Condor2 Pneumatic Tailwheel Fork Unit

Upgrade your RV tailwheel to a smooth-riding, low noise pneumatic tire with our Condor2 system. This listing is for a complete retrofit unit and includes the Condor2 Fork, aluminum hub, 200×50 6-ply Aero Classic Tire and Tost Aero tube.

Please note: though it looks similar, the Condor2 fork has different dimensions than the Doug Bell tailwheel. The Bell fork, and other forks designed for the standard 6″ wheel, are not large enough to accommodate the 200×50 tire.

In addition to the benefits of the pneumatic tire, the 200×50 tire is nearly 8 inches in diameter, lending your airplane maximum tailwheel obstacle clearance and raising the tailwheel for improved visibility over-the-nose. Using the same 3/8″ axle bolt that is standard on Van’s equipment allows you to easily swap out to a solid tire in the event of a flat.

Read a pilot report of this unit here.

For more information on installation, maintenance, and flying with your new tailwheel, we suggest you check out our free

Please be aware that pneumatic tires can and do go flat, and a smaller tire is somewhat more prone to this problem than your larger main tires. Even with the best tires and tubes available, you should expect and be prepared for the occasional flat. We recommend purchasing extra tubes and/or keeping a solid or foam-filled spare on hand in case it is needed.

recs.title: Reusable Oil Filter
recs.detail:
The filter element is made from medical grade, type 304 stainless steel micronic filter cloth providing unmatched protection against oil contamination and resultant engine damage.
A rare earth magnet is installed in the top of the element for magnetic pre-filtering of the oil. The unique twist lock design allows for easy disassembly, inspection and cleaning. The quad-ring gasket doubles the seal between the filter and the engine . The filter housing is carved out of a solid piece of 6061 T6 billet aluminum with cooling fins, which not only looks good but aids in dissipating heat.

recs.title: AirGizmos Gust Lock
recs.detail: Observed rudder wind damage. While traditional tiedowns anchor your airframe to the ramp, unconstrained flight controls remain highly vulnerable to wind-driven squalls and gust loads that cause severe structural wear. The AirGizmos Universal Gust Lock offers lightweight, portable protection designed to lock virtually any control surface securely in place, featuring soft rubber cushions that safeguard your paint and finish from scratches. By preventing control surfaces from violently slamming against their mechanical stops, it eliminates hidden stress that bends hinges, stretches control cables, and damages delicate torque tubes or pushrods. Outfitted with high-visibility colors and an integrated "Remove Before Flight" streamer for fail-safe pre-flight awareness, this simple preventative measure protects you from multi-thousand-dollar sheet metal repair bills and unexpected grounding, giving you total peace of mind whenever your aircraft is parked outdoors.
recs.broch:
AIRGIZMOS UNIVERSAL GUST LOCK

If you fly for very long you will quickly realize the importance of locking your control surfaces when leaving the plane outdoors. Finally we have a solution. The AirGizmos Gust Locks are designed to quickly lock virtually any control surface securely. Its bright color and integrated flag reminds you to remove before flight. The rubber cushions ensure that your finish will be protected. They are lightweight and portable. Perfect for carrying in the plane wherever you go.

squawks.title: Smoke system install not optimized
squawks.detail:
For optimal smoke production, injector nozzles should be placed as far forward (after the first exhaust elbow) as possible increasing exposure time to heat to ensure maximum atomization.  

Incorrect placement will result in unvaporized smoke oil increasing belly contamination. 

Check valves to be installed as close to injector nozzles as practical to prevent syphoning and ensure immediate cutoff. Failure to do so creates trailing smoke after switch deactivation.

squawks.title: Aileron jam nut backed off
squawks.detail:
Right wing aileron rod end bearing jam nut not engaged. 

When a jam nut isn't torqued down, loads are no longer transferred through the nut shoulder and instead focus directly on the root of the exposed threads. This stress concentration, combined with constant vibration, leads to rapid fatigue failure that can cause the rod end shank to snap completely in two, resulting in an immediate mechanical disconnect and potential total loss of control.

Stripped screws on inspection panels.
squawks.res: Installed QTY 12 AN507C832R8 SS machine screws on left/right underwing inspection panel.  Tightened right wing rod end bearing jam nut in accordance with 43.13 Table 7-1.

squawks.title: Engine driven fuel pump drain capped
squawks.detail:
Engine driven fuel pump drain capped with red plug. 

If the internal fuel diaphragm fails, trapped fuel is forced past the engine oil seal directly into the crankcase. Avgas dilutes the oil, destroying lubrication and risking in-flight engine seizure.

The line also serves as an atmospheric reference vent. Capping it traps air and fuel inside the cavity, building pressure that restricts the diaphragm's stroke and causes fluctuating fuel pressure or fuel starvation at high RPM.
squawks.res: Removed engine driven fuel vent plug to allow for proper diaphragm ventilation.

CONDITION INSPECTION — ENGINE
Date: 31 Aug 2026       Reg: N66BA/N907HR
Make: LYCOMING    Model: IO-540-A4D5/EXP    S/N: L-21820-40A
Tach: 62.4    Hobbs: 208.3    ATTIS: 142.0    TSMOH: 62.4    TSPOH: 62.4

- Removed electric fuel pump and Installed Dukes PN: 4140-00-17 SN: 7928 electric fuel pump, overhauled by Aeromotors LLC WO#M2604239.
- Fabricated aluminum patch for cracked baffling under number 1 cylinder and riveted in place.
- Tightened fuel servo nuts on heim bearing control ends and cotter keyed castellated nut.
- Retimed L/R magneto to 25* BTDC per dataplate in accordance with E-mag V200-6XL.040 installation manual.
- Removed engine driven fuel vent plug to allow for proper diaphragm ventilation.
- Removed fuel selector, cleaned one way valve and lubricated with fuel lube.  Reassembled and verified proper orientation, rotation resistance, and detents.
- Removed fuel servo inlet screen.  Cleaned mesh screen.  Reassembled.
- Removed coking from AntiSplat vacuum exhaust adapter.
- Replaced left/right exhaust hangars with Walker Exhaust Hangar 35143.
- Removed 12 spark plugs and photographed firing ends of all plugs. Installed 12 BR8ES spark plugs, 12 spark plug gaskets 07-0087.  Applied copper based antisieze and torqued to 18ft lbs in accordance with Emag V 200-6XL .042 installation and maintenance manual.
- Removed engine oil suction screen for inspection. Visual check revealed clean wire mesh with zero metal shavings, carbon flakes, or foreign matter present. Cleaned, reinstalled with new AN900-16  copper crush gasket, and safety wired per maintenance manual.
- Oil filter element cut and pleats spread for examination; no metallic contamination or foreign matter observed. Torqued replacement filter to 18ft lbs. Serviced with 10 quarts Phillips 20W50XC. Engine ran. Leak check completed.

Engine inspected as part of the condition inspection performed this date in accordance with the scope and detail of appendix D to part 43.
